issues.description: The problem statement requires a Bookstore initializer with the signature init(books: [Book]) (problem_statement.md lines 9-12). In the solution, Bookstore is implemented with an extra parameter init(books: [Book], valid: Bool) which does not match the specified signature. Additionally, the solution's assembleBookstore() calls Bookstore(books: books) (Client.swift) which is inconsistent with the implemented initializer. This mismatch creates confusion about the required constructor and leads to a structural inconsistency between the specification and the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bookstore initializer match the specification by removing the extra parameter so the signature is init(books: [Book]). Update the implementation accordingly (remove or ignore the 'valid' parameter) and ensure all call sites (e.g. assembleBookstore) construct Bookstore using only the books parameter. Alternatively, if an extra parameter is required by design, update the problem statement and template to document the additional parameter and its purpose consistently.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a Bookstore initializer with the signature init(books: [Book]). The solution defines an initializer init(books: [Book], valid: Bool) (an extra parameter named 'valid'), creating a mismatch between the specified API and the implemented API. This difference breaks the direct mapping from the exercise specification to the implementation and will confuse students about the required initializer signature (and causes the solution's own call sites to be inconsistent).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Bookstore initializer with the problem statement by removing the extraneous 'valid' parameter. Implement init(books: [Book]) in the Bookstore class and update any call sites to use that signature.
